memoryText: I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read John 8:12 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Jesus says this in the temple courts during the Feast of Booths, when the great lamps were lit. It is one of the seven great “I AM” statements of John’s Gospel.

“I am the light of the world.” The claim is huge. Not a light, but the light. Not of Israel only, but of the world. In the Bible, light is the first thing God created, and it is a picture of his holiness, truth, and life. Jesus says he is that light in person.

“Whoever follows me.” Light is for walking by. It is not enough to admire it. Following means putting one foot in front of the other behind him, trusting him with the path.

“Will not walk in darkness.” Darkness means sin, ignorance, and death. The one who follows Jesus is not left to stumble. Even when the path is hard, he is not lost.

“But will have the light of life.” He will not only see by the light, he will have it, as his own possession. The light is life itself. Jesus does not just show the way; he gives life.

When you feel confused or lost, say this verse. He is the light, and you do not have to find the way alone.
weekInReview: This week Jesus fed five thousand and declared himself the bread of life, and you heard Peter say, “To whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.” At the Feast of Booths he offered living water and said, “Neither do I condemn you” to a woman caught in sin. He declared himself the light of the world, promised that the Son sets us free indeed, and used the divine name of himself: “Before Abraham was, I am.” In the Psalms you read about delighting in God’s word as a lamp for your feet (Psalm 119), and you prayed for light and truth to lead you out of discouragement (Psalm 43). In John 9 and 10 you watched a blind man receive sight and worship, and heard Jesus say that he is the door and the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said, “I am the bread of life.” What do you tend to hunger for in place of him, and what would it mean to feed on him this week?
The woman caught in adultery heard, “Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.” How does the order, grace first and then a call to change, shape how you deal with your own sin?
Jesus is the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep. What does it mean for you personally that he knows you by name?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for being the light, the bread, the door, and the good shepherd.
Tell him which of these you most need today.
